title: Quick check: Performance Auditing and Optimization Workflow

questions.prompt: In the context of “Performance Auditing and Optimization Workflow” and “Establishing a baseline”, What is the first step when optimizing a slow page?
options: Measure a baseline and identify the bottleneck before choosing a fix.
Rewrite every component without collecting evidence.
Add more dependencies before understanding the bottleneck.
Assume all slowness comes from CSS.
questions.answer_key: Measure a baseline and identify the bottleneck before choosing a fix.
questions.explanation: Optimization should be evidence-driven: measure, identify, change, and measure again.

questions.prompt: While implementing “Performance Auditing and Optimization Workflow”, How can a page reduce unnecessary client JavaScript?
options: Mark all modules as client-only regardless of use.
Import every feature on the first render.
Prefer Server Components for non-interactive composition and lazy-load genuinely optional client code.
Move secrets to the client to avoid server code.
questions.answer_key: Prefer Server Components for non-interactive composition and lazy-load genuinely optional client code.
questions.explanation: Server-first composition and careful splitting can reduce the browser bundle and improve startup work.

questions.prompt: When reviewing “Performance Auditing and Optimization Workflow”, How should performance improvements be reported?
options: Compare the same meaningful metric under comparable conditions and include trade-offs.
Claim a percentage without recording any baseline.
Compare unrelated devices and request paths.
Ignore accessibility and correctness to optimize one metric.
questions.answer_key: Compare the same meaningful metric under comparable conditions and include trade-offs.
questions.explanation: Measurements need a consistent baseline and must not substitute performance for correct behavior.
